newsitem.title: USA: J. Ray McDermott sees improved FY 1998.
newsitem.headline: J. Ray McDermott sees improved FY 1998.

text.p: J. Ray McDermott said Friday it expects improved results in fiscal 1998, following a difficult year in fiscal 1997.

The company, which is majority-owned by McDermott International Inc, reported a loss of $56.7 million, or $1.44 per in ithe fourth quarter, which ended March 31, and a loss of $4.1 million, or $0.28 per share, for the full year.
The company said that while its volume of activity for the year exceeded fiscal 1996 levels, many projects carried low profit margins.

"Although certain of these projects will continue to dampen fiscal 1998 results," said chief executive Roger Tetrault, "we believe that fiscal 1998 will be a better year than fiscal 1997. Our consolidated backlog was $1.8 billion at March 31, 1997 compared with $1.0 billion a year earlier."
He said the company has recently experienced some improvement in pricing.
The company also noted its previously announced internal investigation of allegations of wrongdoing by some former employees is continuing with the aid of outside legal counsel.
